title: The merge hook judges new queue records by the old schema
what: The merge hook checks the queue records of the incoming tree with the record rules of that same tree (its lib/relay_queue.py, read from the branch's commit, not from the hook's own copy), so a change of the record schema together with its records can merge; records malformed by the incoming tree's own rules are still refused; everything else the hook checks is unchanged and still comes from the hook's own code.
why: 26 Oct, live: `git -C ~/relay merge --ff-only wt/where-list` (the owner's "a" on `where` as a list, ready: gate green, check open 0) was refused "queue item a-project-added-by-setup-cannot-be-removed-again is malformed (where is not a string)": master's hook reads the branch's list-form records with master's string rule. No schema change of queue records can ever merge. IP chosen by the front (agent-chosen), above where-list's merge.
failing_case: A temporary repo: master with string-form records and the current hook; a branch whose lib/relay_queue.py accepts only list-form `where` and whose records are lists; the hook refuses the ff-only merge as malformed.
pass_cases: The same merge passes the record check; a branch whose records break its own lib's rules is still refused; a branch that changes no lib is judged as today.
where: plugins/core/hooks/merge.py:166 (the queue record check), plugins/core/lib/relay_queue.py (the copy it imports)
